documentary.title: The Black Death: How 12 Ships Brought the Plague to Europe

shorts.title: The Ships of Death
shorts.hook: Twelve ships sailed into a harbor in Sicily. Almost everyone on board was dead.

shorts.title: The Plague Doctor Myth
shorts.hook: The famous beaked plague mask didn’t exist during the Black Death. It showed up about 300 years later.

shorts.title: The Siege of Caffa
shorts.hook: In 1346, an army hurled dead bodies over a city wall.

shorts.title: Ring Around the Rosie
shorts.hook: You’ve heard this nursery rhyme is about the plague. There’s no evidence it is.

shorts.title: The Flagellants
shorts.hook: Thousands of people marched across Europe whipping themselves bloody, believing it would stop the plague.

shorts.title: Quarantine Was Born Here
shorts.hook: The word quarantine comes from the Italian for forty days.

shorts.title: The Plague Made Workers Rich
shorts.hook: After the Black Death, peasants suddenly had something new: bargaining power.

documentary.title: Pompeii: The Last 24 Hours of a Roman City

shorts.title: The Plaster Bodies
shorts.hook: The bodies of Pompeii aren’t bodies. They’re hollows in the ash, filled with plaster.

shorts.title: We Had the Date Wrong
shorts.hook: For centuries we had the date of Pompeii’s destruction wrong.

shorts.title: Pliny Sailed Toward It
shorts.hook: When Vesuvius erupted, one Roman admiral sailed straight toward it.

shorts.title: Roman Fast Food
shorts.hook: Romans grabbed fast food too, and archaeologists found the counter.

shorts.title: 81 Loaves in the Oven
shorts.hook: In one Pompeii bakery, archaeologists found 81 loaves still in the oven.

shorts.title: The Walls Talk
shorts.hook: Pompeii’s walls are covered in 2,000-year-old graffiti. Some of it is very rude.

shorts.title: Herculaneum’s Last Seconds
shorts.hook: In the town next door, it was over in moments.

documentary.title: The Fall of Constantinople: The Last Day of the Roman Empire
chapters: A City of a Thousand Years

shorts.title: The Cannon Nobody Bought
shorts.hook: The engineer offered his giant cannon to the Byzantines first. They couldn’t afford it.

shorts.title: Ships Over a Hill
shorts.hook: A chain blocked the sultan’s navy, so he moved his ships over land.

shorts.title: The Sultan Was 21
shorts.hook: The man who ended the Roman Empire was 21 years old.

shorts.title: The Gate Left Open
shorts.hook: One story says the city fell because someone left a small gate open.

shorts.title: The Emperor Who Vanished
shorts.hook: The last Roman emperor charged into battle and was never seen again.

shorts.title: Rome Lasted Until 1453
shorts.hook: The Roman Empire didn’t end in 476. Half of it lasted almost another thousand years.

shorts.title: The Day the Middle Ages Ended
shorts.hook: Many historians mark the end of the Middle Ages with one day in 1453.

documentary.title: The Salem Witch Trials: How a Town Turned on Itself

shorts.title: Nobody Was Burned
shorts.hook: No one was burned at the stake in Salem.

shorts.title: It Started With Two Girls
shorts.hook: In January 1692, two girls in a minister’s house began having fits.

shorts.title: More Weight
shorts.hook: Giles Corey was crushed under stones for two days. Legend says he only asked for more weight.

shorts.title: The Moldy Bread Theory
shorts.hook: Some researchers think Salem’s ‘witchcraft’ may have started with moldy rye.

shorts.title: Convicted by a Ghost
shorts.hook: In Salem, you could be convicted because someone said your spirit attacked them.

shorts.title: The Dogs of Salem
shorts.hook: Even two dogs were killed during the Salem panic.

shorts.title: Cleared in 2022
shorts.hook: The last Salem ‘witch’ wasn’t officially cleared until 2022.
